correctness.rationale: For even N at least eight and every real x>0, the weighted Laplacian splits orthogonally into constant, pair-symmetric mean-zero, and pair-antisymmetric eigenvectors. Exact representatives produce all matching/nonmatching columns. The absolute-current counts account for the sole sign change at x=1; P diagonals are strictly below one. The two orbit differences factor into positive denominators and linear threshold polynomials. Direct differentiation gives their isolated maxima, and explicit inequalities dominate every competing branch. Exact-grounded rational computations independently check 1,840 columns, including phase boundary equalities. No numerical inference is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The complete graph is a natural dense electrical network; giving one perfect matching a second positive conductance is a canonical symmetry-preserving perturbation. The exact norms have genuinely distinct edge-orbit transitions, a long conductance interval where complementary projections maximize on opposite classes, a dimension-eight exception, and separate optimizing weights with the same sharp square-root-order amplification for every even N>=10. These are structural operator-space phenomena, not just a numerical table or reparameterization.
